metadata.title: Nook
metadata.tagline: A private place for the things you need to keep.
metadata.summary: Nook is a deliberately simple, private vault for the credentials and sensitive information you choose to keep close. It encrypts your vault before storing it on your device, requires no account or cloud service, and gives you control over your own backups.
metadata.overview: Nook is a deliberately simple, private vault for the credentials and sensitive information you choose to keep close. It encrypts your vault before storing it on your device, requires no account or cloud service, and gives you control over your own backups.
metadata.why: I wanted a password manager that felt like a small personal vault rather than another cloud service. Nook started as an experiment in building a genuinely useful offline-first Flutter application, but quickly became an exploration of local encryption, secure storage, lifecycle protection, and thoughtful privacy-focused UX.
features: Login, bank account, Wi-Fi, API, identity & card templates
challenges: Designing a flexible schema system without making every entry form unnecessarily complex.
Building encrypted persistence around a user-controlled master password.
Handling app lifecycle events without exposing an unlocked vault.
Making backups useful while keeping them encrypted.
Importing Google Password Manager data without creating unnecessary plaintext copies.
Managing asynchronous operations safely across Flutter's navigation and lifecycle system.
lessons: Designed a security-sensitive Flutter application around clear cryptographic boundaries.
Learned to treat application lifecycle and navigation as part of the security model.
Built encrypted local persistence and authenticated backup/restore flows.
Designed reusable schema-driven forms instead of hard-coding every entry type.
Learned how platform-specific Android behavior can affect an otherwise cross-platform Flutter application.
Tested the application beyond the happy path using automated tests and real-device release builds.
